result.title: Measure Less, Know More: Self-Supervised Test-Time Feature Acquisition
result.summary: Recent progress in multimodal, high-dimensional learning has enabled foundation models to process heterogeneous, large-scale data. However, at test time, acquiring all features or modalities can be prohibitively costly and often redundant. Sequentially selecting informative modalities is therefore critical, yet challenging when the downstream task or prediction target is unknown. To this end, we introduce ECHO-$k$, a task-agnostic and self-supervised learning principle for modality acquisition: we use a deep model's internal pretrained representations (e.g., from a foundation model) as proxy targets that summarize cross-modal information. We provide theoretical guarantees in a stylized linear setting that motivate a reinforcement learning (RL) policy for sequential modality selection. Across task-agnostic and label-free acquisition baselines, ECHO-$k$ consistently improves budgeted downstream performance across diverse foundation-model backends. Our method provides a principled route to cost-aware test-time deployment, with implications for any multimodal system where measurements are expensive or time-constrained, and downstream tasks unknown a priori.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 ECHO-k：在任务未知、无标签的测试时，用预训练深度模型内部表征作为跨模态信息的代理目标，并以强化学习策略按预算顺序选择模态；线性设定下给出理论保证。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「按预算顺序获取模态、以内部表征为代理目标」的机制，可能与 LVR 中 LOOK/STOP 的决策与视觉证据筛选、以及训练信号如何指向任务必要信息这一问题直接相关，值得核查其 RL 停止准则能否迁移到 latent 推理的证据获取。
